subject: Deletion trigger mapping & cross-cloud retention clarifications for marketplace deal
messages:
From: Sofia Patel <sofia.patel@stratusbridge.com>
To: priyom.d@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 7 Dec 2027 10:12:00 -0800
Subject: Data deletion triggers and regional retention — requirements for marketplace listing

Hi Priyom,

Thanks for the walkthrough earlier. As we start the compliance review for the Marketplace listing, legal and ops want a clear mapping of how deletion requests and retention policies will be enforced across AWS/GCP/Azure for our customers. A few concrete asks to help us close the procurement checklist:

- How is a customer-initiated deletion propagated to different cloud providers when a tenant spans multiple regions (e.g., US-West on AWS, europe-west on GCP)?
- Can Redwood guarantee deletion within X hours for data stored in partner-managed S3/GCS/Azure Blob backends?
- Do you support retention holds / legal-hold overrides per-account or per-tenant (and how are they scoped across regions)?

Attached: StratusBridge_Data_Location_Specs.pdf (spreadsheet with a sample of our customer location footprints)

We'd appreciate short answers we can pass to procurement and legal. Happy to hop on a quick call.

Thanks,
Sofia Patel
Head of Platform Security
StratusBridge
From: Priyom Das <priyom.d@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Patel <sofia.patel@stratusbridge.com>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 7 Dec 2027 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Data deletion triggers and regional retention — requirements for marketplace listing

Hi Sofia — thanks for the clear list. Short answers below; I added a few follow-ups where we need example triggers.

- Propagation: Redwood maintains a global control plane that records deletion requests at the tenancy level. For cross-cloud tenants we orchestrate deletion by sending region-specific delete jobs to the host adapters for the relevant storage backends (S3/GCS/Blob). We track per-object deletion status in our audit log and expose job-level progress via the Console API.

- SLA for deletion: We can commit to a standard 72-hour window for coordinated deletion across supported clouds for medium-sized datasets. For very large datasets or archival tiers, we provide a time estimate and a progress report. If your contract needs a stricter SLA (e.g., 24 hours) we'll need a dedicated reserved capacity clause (helps prioritize deletion jobs).

- Retention holds: We support per-tenant retention holds. Holds are honored at the control plane level and block automated deletion workflows until cleared by an authorized principal. Holds are enforced regardless of the storage provider; the control plane prevents issuing delete jobs against held objects.

Follow-ups we need from you:
1) Example deletion triggers (customer portal request vs API vs DocuSign legal request) — attach two lines from your sample that represent your primary triggers.
2) A rough percent split of data per cloud/provider so we can model parallel deletion execution.

I've attached a quick mapping workbook (RBW-deletion-mapping-draft.xlsx) with columns for trigger type, region, cloud provider, and suggested SLO buckets — please review and populate where you can.

Plan: If helpful, Ben can scope the change to our runbook and Marissa can surface the audit logs we'll share with your team.

Thanks,
Priyom Das
Senior Partnerships Manager
Redwood Inference
From: Sofia Patel <sofia.patel@stratusbridge.com>
To: priyom.d@redwood.ai
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 7 Dec 2027 13:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Data deletion triggers and regional retention — requirements for marketplace listing

Thanks, Priyom — helpful.

Quick clarifications:
- Primary deletion trigger will be 'Customer Portal -> Delete Account' (interactive) and 'Legal hold release via signed DocuSign' (non-interactive). We will send an API webhook in a subset of cases.
- EU-specific requirement: if a European customer issues deletion, we need proof of deletion and a 180-day legal-hold option (court/authority requests) that can be applied retroactively to prevent automated purges. That hold needs to be scoped to EU tenants only.

Attached: SB-Residency-Constraints.csv (sample rows for EU/US accounts)

We're okay with 72 hours as a starting point; procurement will flag if the contract needs a 24-hour commit. DocuSign for the legal workflow: https://app.docusign.com/embedded/abcdef123456

Can you confirm where in the audit log a note that 'legal_hold_applied' would appear (field name is fine)? Also confirm whether you can surface the per-object deletion job id in the console so our ops can reconcile.

Sofia
Sofia Patel
Head of Platform Security
StratusBridge
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Patel <sofia.patel@stratusbridge.com>
Cc: priyom.d@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 7 Dec 2027 16:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Data deletion triggers and regional retention — requirements for marketplace listing

Hi Sofia — short answers and next steps below.

- 'legal_hold_applied' is an event stored on the tenant record in the control plane; it appears in audit logs as event.type=LEGAL_HOLD with metadata.hold_scope=region:EU (or region:GLOBAL). We will provide the exact sample log lines in the runbook.

- Per-object deletion job IDs: yes — every deletion run produces a job id (format: deljob-<uuid>) and we persist job -> object mapping for 365 days by default (can be extended per contract). The Console and the Console API expose job status and a downloadable CSV for reconciliation.

Action items (we'll take the lead):
1) Priyom: finalize the RBW deletion mapping workbook with your cloud-split numbers (due Thu 2027-12-09).
2) Marissa: assemble a 1-page runbook excerpt showing sample audit log lines and where to find deljob IDs; attach RBW-residency-playbook-v1.docx.
3) Ben: prepare optional 24-hour SLA language and impact notes for procurement.

We'll update the HubSpot deal record: https://hubspot.example/deal/3421

If you can add two rows to the RBW workbook with (a) 'Customer Portal' and (b) 'DocuSign legal release' as triggers that will help us close the procurement checklist faster.

Thanks — happy to jump on a 30-min call if you prefer to walk through.

Best,
Ben Carter
Head of Marketplace Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Attachments: RBW-residency-playbook-v1.docx
